Fix NCDatasets extension for Julia 1.12 (#127)

* Fix NCDatasets extension for Julia 1.12 incremental compilation

Replace __init__ + @eval pattern with a direct import and compile-time
method definition for default_output_attributes. The old pattern broke
incremental compilation on Julia 1.12 because eval into a closed module
is no longer allowed.

Requires Oceananigans >= 0.106.4 (CliMA/Oceananigans.jl#5469).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Move default_output_attributes to main module

Address review feedback: move default_output_attributes(::SeaIceModel)
and helper functions from the NCDatasets extension to the main ClimaSeaIce
module. With Oceananigans#5469, default_output_attributes is a stub in
Oceananigans.OutputWriters, so the method can be defined at compile time
without needing the NCDatasets extension. Uses qualified name instead of
import.

(0.5.0) Share phase_transitions and bulk densities at the model level (#134)

* Share phase_transitions and bulk densities at the model level

Moves phase_transitions onto SeaIceModel as a shared parameter and
introduces ice_density and snow_density as top-level bulk fields. The
per-layer SlabThermodynamics is slimmed to the state that is genuinely
layer-specific (surface T, heat BCs, raw internal-flux coefficient,
concentration evolution).

latent_heat is rewritten as a per-mass function; tendency kernels
multiply externally by the appropriate bulk density. This fixes the
sign error in the Stefan correction and separates the mass-budget role
of rho from its microscopic role inside L(T).

Removes the sea_ice_model.jl rebuild hack: the combined snow+ice flux
and the snow-ice interface temperature are now computed inline in the
layered kernel, so neither slab's top BC is rewritten at construction
time.

Adds an internal-flux extension mechanism: users can plug in
ConductiveFlux, a bare Function, a pre-assembled FluxFunction, or a
custom struct via `flux_kernel` dispatch.

Resolves CliMA/ClimaSeaIce.jl#133.

(0.5.5) Save SemiImplicitStress caches across checkpoint (#151)

* Add failing test for SemiImplicitStress checkpoint round-trip

`SemiImplicitStress` (used for ice-ocean and ice-atmosphere drag) caches
its per-cell implicit-stress coefficients in `τᵢᵤ`/`τᵢᵥ` Fields. They
are written by `compute_implicit_stress_coefficients!` inside the EVP
substep loop and read by `_compute_sea_ice_ocean_stress!` (via
`implicit_τx_coefficient`) every time the coupled `update_state!`
runs — including the call triggered by `initialize_simulation!` on a
restored simulation.

`prognostic_state(::SeaIceMomentumEquation)` currently only walks
`auxiliaries.fields` and skips `external_momentum_stresses`, so these
caches do not round-trip. In a coupled simulation this manifests as
~1e-9-per-step drift in ocean velocities after a checkpoint restore.

This commit adds a focused test that exposes the bug directly without
needing a coupled ocean. It currently fails with 4/6 assertions failing.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Save SemiImplicitStress caches in SeaIceMomentumEquation checkpoint state

`prognostic_state(::SeaIceMomentumEquation)` previously only walked
`auxiliaries.fields`. `SemiImplicitStress` caches per-cell implicit-stress
coefficients in its `τᵢᵤ`/`τᵢᵥ` Fields, which are read by
`_compute_sea_ice_ocean_stress!` every time `update_state!` runs (including
on `initialize_simulation!` of a restored sim). Without round-tripping
them, restored simulations drift ~1e-9 per step relative to a no-restart
reference.

Extend `prognostic_state` to also serialize each entry's cache (top and
bottom), with a `hasproperty` check in `restore_prognostic_state!` for
backwards-compatibility with older checkpoint files.

Bumps version 0.5.4 → 0.5.5.
